title: Elevated ICP / cerebral herniation
presentation: Fixed/dilated pupil, extensor posturing, Cushing triad (HTN + bradycardia + irregular respirations), acute decline in GCS
definitions: Uncal: medial temporal lobe over tentorial edge → ipsilateral dilated pupil, contralateral hemiparesis
Central: downward displacement of diencephalon → small reactive pupils then fixed midposition, Cheyne-Stokes
Subfalcine: cingulate gyrus under falx → ACA compression / leg weakness
Tonsillar: cerebellar tonsils through foramen magnum → apnea, bradycardia, death
Normal ICP <15 mm Hg (adults); treatment threshold ≥20–22 mm Hg

immediateActions.action: Call neurosurgery STAT. Position head midline, elevate head of bed 30°
Ensure airway/ventilation — brief mild hyperventilation (target PaCO2 30–35 mm Hg) ONLY as temporizing bridge
Osmotherapy bolus (hypertonic saline preferred over mannitol in hypotension / hypovolemia)
Stat noncontrast head CT (or directly to OR if herniating with known surgical lesion)

notes: Look for midline shift, effaced basal cisterns, hydrocephalus, mass lesion

workup.test: BMP with Na, K, BUN, Cr
notes: Baseline before osmotherapy; recheck q4–6h during therapy
Target PaCO2 35–40 mm Hg; 30–35 only during acute herniation

indication: If intracranial hemorrhage or surgical candidate

treatment.doseText: 250–500 mL IV bolus over 10–20 min (or 2–5 mL/kg, max 500 mL); central line preferred, peripheral acceptable in emergency

dose.label: Bolus
frequency: May repeat bolus if ICP remains elevated and serum Na <155–160 mEq/L

notes: No serum sodium target is endorsed (Cook 2020): SAH — symptom-based boluses rather than a sodium target; ICH — bolus or targeted sodium both acceptable; TBI/AIS — no target recommended. Studies that targeted sodium used 145–155 mEq/L
Ceiling: Na 155–160 mEq/L and Cl 110–115 mEq/L may be reasonable to limit AKI; monitor Na, Cl and renal function (Cook 2020)
Preferred over mannitol if hypotensive (SBP <90) or hypovolemic
Peripheral administration of 3% is safe emergently; switch to central line when placed
evidenceNote: Cook 2020: HTS over mannitol for ICP/edema in TBI — conditional, low-quality evidence; in ICH — conditional, very low
Cook 2020: HTS or mannitol in AIS — conditional, low; neither improves neurological outcome

treatment.doseText: 0.5–1 g/kg IV bolus over 15–30 min through an in-line filter

dose.label: Bolus
frequency: May repeat q4–6h; follow osmolar gap (no validated cutoff) and MAP

notes: Requires Foley catheter — produces vigorous osmotic diuresis

Monitor the osmolar gap rather than serum osmolality (Cook 2020); no gap cutoff is validated — 20 mOsm/kg is used in practice, ≥55 correlated with mannitol concentration in one study; osmolality >320 did not change AKI incidence
Do NOT use if hypotensive or hypovolemic; replace urine volume with isotonic crystalloid if needed
evidenceNote: Cook 2020: mannitol is an effective alternative in TBI when HTS can't be given — conditional, low-quality evidence
Cook 2020: osmolar gap over osmolality for AKI monitoring — conditional, very low

treatment.doseText: 30 mL IV push over 10–15 min through a central line ONLY

dose.label: Bolus
frequency: Reserved for refractory elevated ICP / acute herniation

notes: CENTRAL LINE ONLY — severe tissue necrosis if extravasated
Rapid onset (minutes); keep in ICU / code cart where available

treatment.doseText: 10 mg IV bolus, then 4 mg IV q6h
notes: INDICATED ONLY for vasogenic edema from tumor, abscess, or CNS inflammation
CONTRAINDICATED in acute ischemic stroke, ICH, and traumatic brain injury (CRASH trial showed increased mortality)
evidenceNote: NCCN guidelines (brain metastases); CRASH trial (contraindication in TBI)

treatment.doseText: Titrate to target RASS -4 to -5; avoid hypotension
notes: Reduces cerebral metabolic demand and blunts ICP spikes from coughing/agitation
Propofol infusion syndrome risk with prolonged (>48h) or high-dose (>50 mcg/kg/min) infusions

pitfalls: Do NOT give steroids for ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, or TBI — harmful
Avoid prolonged hyperventilation — causes cerebral vasoconstriction and secondary ischemia; use only as bridge to definitive therapy
Do NOT let serum sodium drop during ICP management — avoid all hypotonic IV fluids (no D5W, no 0.45% NaCl); use 0.9% NaCl as maintenance (Cook 2020: avoid hyponatremia — good practice)
Mannitol in a hypovolemic patient induces severe hypotension, dropping cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP = MAP - ICP)
escalateWhen: Pupillary asymmetry or loss of light reflex
ICP >20–22 mm Hg refractory to first-line osmotherapy
institutionVaries: Availability and stocking of 23.4% NaCl (often restricted to Neuro ICU / code carts)
Osmolar-gap cutoff used to hold mannitol (Cook 2020 prefers the gap over osmolality but sets no cutoff)
Peripheral 3% NaCl protocol (some hospitals permit bolus only, others continuous with concentration limits)
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7
Hawryluk GWJ, et al. Brain Trauma Foundation Guidelines for the Management of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: 2020 Update. Neurosurgery 2020;87:427-434
Roberts I, et al. Effect of intravenous corticosteroids on death within 14 days in 10008 adults with traumatic brain injury (CRASH trial). Lancet 2004;364:1321-1328
